raised_by: NOT raised -- the floor is unchanged at 57 deliberately. What changed is the DENOMINATOR: `total` was 189 and is now 1625, the FULL kind=symbol population, because every such ref is now bucketed instead of silently `continue`d. Measured 2026-08-06: only 193 refs ever reached resolution; 1,122 were dropped for carrying a symbol with no file, 246 for a nonexistent file, 63 for a non-C suffix, 1 for escaping the repo. Every one of those skips ran BEFORE any counting, so retargeting or depairing a ref made the published ratio look BETTER -- a denominator that shrinks as the corpus rots. Coverage did not change; the reported population did. NOTE: `total` is recorded, NOT gated. A second scalar floor would be gamed the same way the first can be (deleting a ref improves it exactly like fixing one); the population invariant is enforced in code instead -- buckets must sum to the occurrence count or the check returns rc 6 rather than publishing a ratio.
why: Check 7 can only inspect a stamped symbol it can RESOLVE; an unresolved ref yields no finding, so losing resolution is indistinguishable from passing. This number is the floor: a drop is an ERROR (rc 7). Raising it is the point -- when the resolver improves, update this file in the same commit and say what changed. This file is TRACKED state and is now enforced fail-CLOSED (rc 8) when missing or malformed; STUB_LINT_ALLOW_NO_BASELINE=1 is the deliberate, reported bypass.
standing_gap: 1,568 occurrences not resolved, in evidence-shaped buckets that deliberately do NOT claim a cause: unpaired-ref 1122 (a symbol named with no file to look in), calllike-unresolved 89 (a `symbol(` token is present in code but the resolver returned nothing), no-calllike-token 47 (no call-like token in that file at all), missing-file 246, non-c-suffix 63, path-escape 1. The names describe what was observed, not why: a call site, a prototype and a macro invocation all carry a call-like token while the real definition lives in another file, so a 'resolver gap' vs 'stale bookkeeping' label would be wrong for a large share of both buckets. Assigning cause needs cross-file definition evidence, which is resolver-coverage work.
largest_recoverable_class: ALL 246 missing-file refs are BARE FILENAMES with no directory component (e.g. `boot_desktop.c:boot_run_deferred`), stored verbatim as repo-relative paths that never exist at the repo root. The files themselves do exist -- boot_desktop.c is src/kernel/main/boot_desktop.c. Of 232 unique such refs, 224 have a UNIQUE basename in the tree, 7 are ambiguous and 1 is absent. That is a larger recoverable class than every other open resolver item combined, and it is owned by the resolver-coverage section of the todo-metadata-layer roadmap.
